fact: The College of Business and Accountancy opened in 1935 as the College of Commerce, with just 20 students.
The first dean of the College was Miss Natividad Sitchon, who led it from 1935 until 1966.
In 1987, CBA was chosen as one of only five pilot schools in entrepreneurship in the whole Philippines.
The name "College of Business and Accountancy" became official on April 1, 2006. Before that, it was the College of Commerce for 71 years.
Central Philippine University was founded in 1905, and its motto "Scientia et Fides" means "Science and Faith".
CHED recognizes CPU as a Center of Excellence in Business Administration. CBA is the only business school in Western Visayas with that designation.
Both BSBA and BS Accountancy hold ACSCU-AAI Level IV re-accreditation, valid until December 2028.
A CPU accountancy graduate placed Top 9 in the October 2023 CPA Licensure Examination.
Every BSBA student completes a 600-hour business internship in their final semester.
BS Entrepreneurship students can specialize in an Agripreneurship, Food Service, or IT track, and implement their own business plan in senior year.
BS Computer Science started in the College of Commerce! It moved to the new College of Computer Studies in SY 2003–2004.
Since 2006, the Accounting Refresher Course has been built into the BS Accountancy curriculum as 24 units of Integrated Review.
To graduate summa cum laude at CPU, you need an Honors Point Average between 1.00 and 1.18.
CPU received PRC awards as a top-performing school in several CPA board exams from May 1999 to October 2006.
Every CBA faculty member holds at least a master's degree.
